tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: [BLOCKER] Values generated by hardcoded display formulas are labelled as AlphaFold3 model output; identical sequences are assigned different pLDDT, which is mathematically impossible for real predictions — Three separate quantities that the UI and README present as AlphaFold3 output are deterministic display formulas with no model behind them. (a) The residue confidence curve plotted under the legend 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score' is 93 + 4*sin(0.4i) + 0.5*(ASCII%5); its analytic range is [89.0, 99.0], so it can never enter the 'High (70-90)', 'Low (50-70)' or 'Very Low (<50)' bins that index.html:389-391 advertises. (b) The 'Predicted Aligned Error' matrix is |i-j|*0.4 + 0.3*(ASCII%4) — symmetric by construction and a monotone function of sequence separation, which real PAE matrices are not. (c) The '3D Structure' is a parametric helix of radius 6.0-9.2 with 0.6 rise per index; I measured its consecutive 'Cα' spacings at min 1.21, max 15.77, mean 6.41 arbitrary units (real Cα-Cα is 3.80 ± 0.04 Å, invariant) — a 1208% bond-length variation, i.e. not a protein backbone. Grep confirms zero `fetch`/XHR/WebSocket calls and zero data files anywhere in the tracked repository (`git ls-files` returns only README.md, app.js, index.html, styles.css, skills-lock.json and the .agents/ skill bundle), so no AlphaFold3 run could have supplied any of it. Independent proof by identity: the 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG appears three times and is assigned pLDDT 92.8 (AF3_CANDIDATES CogAChE-PAS-02, app.js:131), 94.8 (HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2, app.js:156) and 94.3 (BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1, app.js:250). pLDDT is a function of the input; the same monomer sequence cannot yield three different values beyond seed noise of well under 1 unit. I found four such duplicate pairs inside the 25-drug set and seven sequence identities between the 25 drugs and the AF3 top-10 table, every one of them carrying conflicting numbers. Consequence: This is the platform's central claim. A collaborator, reviewer, or investor reading 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score' over a chart, or the code comment 'REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING', will reasonably conclude that AlphaFold3 was run and that the confidence profile reflects model uncertainty. It does not. A design prototype with placeholder data is entirely legitimate; this repository crosses the line because the placeholders are affirmatively labelled with the provenance they lack. Under ICMJE 'B. Scientific Misconduct', data fabrication is 'making up data or results'; presenting formula output under a model's name meets that description if the artefact is ever presented as a research result. Anyone who tried to reproduce these numbers by actually submitting the sequences to AlphaFold Server would get different values and would have grounds to allege fabrication.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Required fix for INTEG-01: Either (a) actually run the sequences (AlphaFold Server or a local AF3/Boltz/Chai deployment), commit the resulting mmCIF plus the per-residue pLDDT and PAE arrays as data files, and render those arrays; or (b) keep the synthetic curves but rename every label so no reader can mistake them: legend `'Illustrative confidence profile (synthetic — not an AlphaFold prediction)'`, panel headings 'Illustrative sequence-parameterised ribbon (not a predicted structure)' and 'Illustrative contact-separation map (not a PAE matrix)', delete the comments at app.js:673, 707 and the word 'Real' at index.html:108, 371, 375, 377 and README.md:108. Additionally, deduplicate the sequences or give identical sequences identical predicted values — the current contradictions are self-falsifying regardless of labelling.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Ground truth for INTEG-01: AlphaFold 3 (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024, doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w) has a confidence head that 'predict[s] a modified local distance difference test (pLDDT) and a predicted aligned error (PAE) matrix as in AF2, as well as a distance error matrix (PDE)', plus pTM/ipTM. These are learned per-token outputs of a diffusion model conditioned on an MSA and template stack; they are not analytic functions of residue index or ASCII code, they are not smooth sinusoids, and PAE is not symmetric. AF3 confidence values are effectively deterministic for a fixed sequence and seed. Real Cα-Cα virtual bond length is 3.80 Å (trans peptide), and an α-helix has a Cα radius of ~2.3 Å with 1.5 Å rise per residue and 3.6 residues/turn — none of which the generator reproduces.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: [BLOCKER] All 25 ΔG/Kd pairs are thermodynamically impossible; the pair was co-generated by a rule implying RT = 1.05 kcal/mol (T = 528 K) with a non-zero intercept, and AlphaFold3 emits no energetic quantity at all — Every one of the 25 candidates reports a ΔG and a Kd side by side. At 298.15 K, RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol and ΔG = RT·ln(Kd). Checking all 25: the stated ΔG is more negative than the stated Kd permits by 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol, i.e. the stated Kd is 665x to 15,729x larger than the stated ΔG implies. Examples: HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 'ΔG = -18.4 kcal/mol | Kd = 0.32 nM' — 0.32 nM corresponds to -12.95 kcal/mol, and -18.4 kcal/mol corresponds to 3.3e-14 M (0.033 pM), a 9,828-fold discrepancy. BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 'ΔG = -19.5 | Kd = 0.08 nM' is off by 15,729x. Regressing ΔG on ln(Kd) across all 25 gives ΔG = 4.682 + 1.0495·ln(Kd) with R² = 0.9939. The near-perfect fit proves the two columns were produced together by a single rule rather than measured or computed independently; the slope 1.0495 implies an 'effective RT' of 1.05 kcal/mol, i.e. T = 528 K (255 °C), and the +4.68 intercept means no temperature whatsoever reconciles them. Separately, the ΔG values themselves are outside the physical envelope: -19.5 kcal/mol implies Kd = 5 fM, tighter than the biotin-streptavidin complex (~10 fM, ΔG ≈ -18.3 kcal/mol), the tightest well-characterised non-covalent protein-ligand interaction known. All 25 candidates are claimed to sit at or beyond that limit. Finally, AF3 does not produce ΔG or Kd under any configuration, so the README's framing of these as products of an AlphaFold3 pipeline has no possible mechanism. Consequence: This is an independent, arithmetic falsification that does not depend on reading the rendering code at all: a reviewer with a calculator can demonstrate in one minute that the affinity table cannot be the output of any method. It converts a 'the labels are overclaimed' concern into a demonstrable internal contradiction. Ranking candidates (the 'Leaderboard', index.html:296) on numbers that are mutually inconsistent means the entire prioritisation is arbitrary — a downstream user selecting X5 over X3 for synthesis would be acting on noise. The 'Peak Binding Energy -19.5 kcal' headline stat (index.html:74-75) is the single most prominent number on the landing page.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Required fix for INTEG-02: Delete the Kd column or derive it: `kd = Math.exp(dG / (R*T))` with T stated on the page. Report only one of the two as primary and mark the other 'derived'. If any ΔG is meant to be real, name the method, software version, force field, and per-value uncertainty (e.g. 'MM-GBSA, AMBER ff19SB/GAFF2, 100 ns, ΔG = -8.2 ± 1.9 kcal/mol, rescoring only — not a binding constant'). Cap claimed affinities at physically defensible values and state explicitly that scoring-function ΔG is not a measured Kd. Add a unit test that fails the build if |ΔG - RT·ln(Kd)| > 0.5 kcal/mol for any record.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Ground truth for INTEG-02: ΔG° = -RT·ln(Ka) = RT·ln(Kd) with R = 1.9872e-3 kcal·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹. At 298.15 K, RT = 0.5925 kcal/mol; at 310 K (body temperature), RT = 0.6160 kcal/mol. 1 nM ⇒ ΔG = -12.28 kcal/mol at 298 K. Neither temperature nor any plausible standard-state convention produces the reported pairs. AlphaFold 3 (Abramson et al., Nature 2024, doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w) outputs coordinates plus pLDDT, PAE, PDE, pTM and ipTM — no energetics. Binding free energy requires a separate method (FEP/TI, MM-GBSA/PBSA, or an empirical scoring function), each with its own error bars; even well-executed alchemical FEP typically carries ~1 kcal/mol RMSE, so a claimed value must always be accompanied by a method, a force field, a sampling protocol, and an uncertainty.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: [CRITICAL] Absolute safety claims ('0% Risk', 'Peripheral Side Effects: None', 'Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%') are asserted for molecules intended for human cognition, with no ADMET model in the repository and a mechanism that is directionally wrong for these sequences — Three distinct defects. (1) Provenance: README.md:98 asserts that screening was performed. There is no ADMET predictor, no hERG model, no immunogenicity tool, no descriptor calculation and no result file anywhere in the repository — the safety fields are literal strings in the same array as the drug names. (2) Expressibility: '0% Risk', 'None', '0.0%' and '100%' are not outputs any predictive method can produce. Every in-silico classifier returns a probability with a decision threshold and a validated applicability domain; a zero is a statement of certainty that no model licenses. (3) Direction: the stated mechanism — that hydrophobic linkers sterically prevent hERG binding — inverts the actual structure-activity relationship. I computed the physicochemistry of the sequences: HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 / BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 (KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG) carry a net charge of +9 at pH 7.4 with 13 Lys/Arg and 31% aromatic (W/F/Y) content; MicroAutophagy-Tag-M4 is +7 with 28% aromatics. Cationic, aromatic-rich, amphipathic sequences are the canonical hERG-blocker pharmacophore and the canonical membrane-lytic/haemolytic peptide motif — the opposite of a safety argument. No haemolysis, no cytotoxicity, and no immunogenicity (MHC-II binding / ADA risk) assessment appears anywhere, despite 24 of 25 candidates being peptides. Consequence: These are nootropic candidates aimed at healthy human cognition, where the safety bar is higher than for oncology, not lower. A '0% cardiotoxicity' claim carried in a README with a DeepMind badge is precisely the kind of statement a non-specialist reader — an angel investor, a supplement formulator, a collaborator, a journalist — would take at face value. If this repository were shown as a pitch, it constitutes a specific, quantified, unsubstantiated safety representation about substances for human consumption. It is also the claim most likely to attract regulatory attention if the project ever moves toward an IND, an NDI notification, or a wellness product, and the most damaging if the underlying formula-generated provenance is later discovered.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Required fix for INTEG-03: Delete every absolute safety statement. If a screen is genuinely wanted, run named tools and record their identity and version (e.g. ADMET-AI, pkCSM, SwissADME, ProtParam plus an MHC-II binding predictor such as NetMHCIIpan for the peptides) and report each result as a probability with the tool's own stated accuracy and applicability domain: `hERG blockade: P = 0.31 (ADMET-AI v1.x, classifier AUC 0.84 on ChEMBL hold-out; peptides are outside the model's small-molecule applicability domain — result not interpretable)`. Explicitly flag that essentially all published hERG and ADMET models are trained on small molecules and are out-of-domain for 30-45mer cationic peptides, so the correct honest output here is 'not assessable with available in-silico models'. Add the missing peptide-specific liabilities (haemolysis, membrane lysis, immunogenicity, protease stability, BBB penetration) as explicit open risks rather than omitting them.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Ground truth for INTEG-03: Tyr652 and Phe656 in the hERG (KCNH2) S6 inner cavity are correctly identified as the principal drug-binding residues (Mitcheson et al., 'A structural basis for drug-induced long QT syndrome', PNAS 2000, doi:10.1073/pnas.210244497, PMID 11005845) — but that paper establishes that binding is driven by aromatic/hydrophobic contact with those residues, typically for cationic amphiphiles. Hydrophobicity and a basic centre increase hERG liability; they do not shield against it. Regulatory hERG assessment is governed by ICH S7B/E14 and requires in-vitro patch clamp, not a computed descriptor. No validated in-silico ADMET model reports a zero-probability outcome; the FDA CM&S credibility framework (see literature) requires that any computational output used as evidence be accompanied by a stated context of use, model risk, and verification/validation evidence commensurate with that risk.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: [CRITICAL] In-vivo efficacy and chronic-dosing outcomes (LTP +280%, ACh +350%, CBF +45%, working memory +240%, tolerance <4.2% at 30 days) are presented as platform results, though no computational method can produce them — The README frames the entire document as the output of an 'AlphaFold3 De Novo Drug Discovery Platform' and then reports two-and-three-significant-figure effect sizes for endpoints that are measured, not predicted: field-EPSP slope potentiation (LTP), Golgi/two-photon spine counting, microdialysis ACh, laser-Doppler or ASL-MRI cerebral blood flow, delayed-response behavioural testing, and lysosomal degradation kinetics. 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days' is a chronic in-vivo pharmacodynamic endpoint requiring 30 days of repeat dosing in an animal model. No structure predictor, docking program, or ADMET tool outputs any of these. There is no methods section, no animal model, no assay, no n, no error bar, no statistical test, and no citation anywhere in the repository. The precision of the figures ('+280%', '<4.2%') is the signature of invented numbers: a real +280% LTP measurement would be reported as, e.g., '278 ± 34% of baseline, n = 8 slices, p = 0.003'. Consequence: These are the numbers that make the project look like it has results rather than a hypothesis. They are the sentences a reader will quote back — 'their lead candidate gives +310% spine density'. A journal would treat unsourced quantitative efficacy claims with no methods as a fabrication concern under ICMJE 'B. Scientific Misconduct'; an institution's research integrity office would open an inquiry on the 30-day tolerance figure alone, because it implies an animal study that did not occur. The same claims in a fundraising or partnering context are material misrepresentations.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Required fix for INTEG-04: Move every efficacy percentage out of the results voice and into an explicitly hypothetical voice, with the experiment that would test it named. E.g. replace 'Neurogenesis & CA1 LTP (+280%)' with 'Design hypothesis: TrkB D5 engagement should enhance CA1 LTP. Untested. Proposed assay: field-EPSP slope in acute hippocampal slices, theta-burst induction, n ≥ 8, vs vehicle.' Add a 'Claim status' column to every candidate with values HYPOTHESIS / IN-SILICO / IN-VITRO / IN-VIVO, and set all 25 to HYPOTHESIS today. Delete 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days' outright — there is no in-silico substitute for it.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Ground truth for INTEG-04: None of AlphaFold 3's outputs (coordinates, pLDDT, PAE, PDE, pTM, ipTM — Abramson et al., Nature 2024) bear on physiological efficacy. Effect sizes at these endpoints come from ex-vivo electrophysiology, in-vivo microdialysis, imaging, and behaviour. Reporting standards for any predictive-model claim in biomedicine require the model, data, evaluation split and metric to be specified (DOME recommendations, Walsh et al., Nat Methods 18:1122-1127, 2021, doi:10.1038/s41592-021-01205-4); reporting standards for any prediction intended to inform clinical decisions require the full TRIPOD+AI item set (Collins et al., BMJ 385:e078378, 2024, doi:10.1136/bmj-2023-078378). The current text satisfies neither because there is no model to report.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: [CRITICAL] 'AlphaFold Server Live Connected' and 'Generated with AlphaFold3' assert a computational integration and a provenance that do not exist in the code — The header badge reads 'AlphaFold Server Live Connected' and the dashboard advertises an 'AF3 Engine' with 'Live AlphaFold Integration'. The implementation is a plain `<a href>` hyperlink to alphafoldserver.com plus a clipboard copy (app.js:660-671). There is no HTTP client, no API key, no request, no response handling, no polling — I confirmed zero network primitives in the entire codebase. A 'Live Connected' status badge is a specific technical assertion about system state, and it is false. The footer goes further: 'Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling' attributes the page's contents to AlphaFold3, which per INTEG-01 never ran. Consequence: A status badge is the one UI element users trust as machine-verified rather than authored. Presenting a static hyperlink as a live connection misrepresents the system's capability to anyone evaluating the platform's technical maturity — which is exactly the audience a demo is built for. Combined with the footer provenance line, a viewer reasonably concludes that the pLDDT curves and ΔG values on screen came off an AlphaFold3 run. This is the mechanism by which an internal prototype becomes an external misrepresentation without anyone intending it.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Ground truth for INTEG-05: AlphaFold Server has no public programmatic API for third-party submission; the documented workflow is manual upload through the web UI. A truthful description of what this code does is: 'copies the sequence to your clipboard and opens AlphaFold Server in a new tab, where you can paste it and run the prediction yourself.' That workflow is genuinely useful and is the honest version of the claim.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: [MAJOR] Google DeepMind branding, an AlphaFold3 shield badge with the Google logo, and the repository name imply an affiliation and endorsement that do not exist, while AlphaFold Server's terms restrict use — The README's first badge renders as a for-the-badge shield reading 'AlphaFold3 | DeepMind Server' carrying the Google logo, and the application header subtitle reads 'DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform' — a construction that parses as 'this is a DeepMind platform', not 'this platform uses AlphaFold'. The project directory is literally named DeepMind_Bio. Nowhere in README.md, index.html or app.js is there any disclaimer of affiliation (grep for 'disclaim|not affiliated' returns nothing across all four files). Separately, the README declares a 'Private Research' licence but does not state a use restriction inherited from the tool it advertises: AlphaFold Server output is licensed for non-commercial use only, and holders must not use it on behalf of a commercial organisation or in automated systems predicting protein-ligand interactions. A platform that describes itself as a 'drug discovery platform' generating ranked therapeutic candidates is squarely in the territory those terms restrict — a point the repository never engages with. Consequence: If this repository is made public, shown to an investor, or attached to a grant or partnering deck, the Google/DeepMind visual identity plus the absence of a disclaimer creates a false impression of institutional backing for the '0% Risk' safety claims and the candidate rankings. That is the compounding harm: the borrowed credibility attaches specifically to the numbers that are least supportable. It also exposes the author to a trademark/attribution complaint that is entirely avoidable, and — if the project ever commercialises — to a terms-of-use conflict on any AlphaFold Server output actually incorporated.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Required fix for INTEG-06: Replace the badge at README.md:3 with a neutral one (`![Uses AlphaFold Server](https://img.shields.io/badge/uses-AlphaFold_Server-blue)`, no Google logo, no 'DeepMind' in the label). Change index.html:30 to 'Structural Pharmacology & De Novo Design Prototype'. Rename the directory away from DeepMind_Bio. Add verbatim to README.md immediately under the title: 'This project is an independent effort and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or connected to Google DeepMind or Google LLC. AlphaFold is a trademark of Google DeepMind. No AlphaFold Server output is contained in this repository. If AlphaFold Server output is added in future, it will be used only under the AlphaFold Server Output Terms of Use, which permit non-commercial use only.' Add a proper citation of Abramson et al., Nature 2024, doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Ground truth for INTEG-06: AlphaFold is a Google DeepMind trademark. AlphaFold Server Output Terms of Use state the output is available free of charge for non-commercial use only, that only individuals and non-commercial organisations may use it, that users must not use the Server, Output or Derivatives on behalf of a commercial organisation or in connection with commercial activities including research on behalf of commercial organisations, and that Google reserves the right to require deletion of Output. The separate AlphaFold 3 model-parameter terms and prohibited-use policy impose further constraints on self-hosted use. Standard practice for third-party tools built on a vendor model is an explicit non-affiliation notice plus a citation of the model paper.

text: [MAJOR] The candidate dataset is internally contradictory and partly not chemistry: identical sequences carry conflicting targets and numbers, three sequences contain the non-standard residue 'B', and one 'FASTA sequence' is an English phrase that the pLDDT chart happily plots — Four defects in the underlying data model. (1) Four sequence pairs are byte-identical yet are asserted to bind entirely unrelated proteins with different residue contacts, and are given different ΔG, Kd and pLDDT — e.g. CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH is simultaneously a 'Frizzled-8 CRD activator' (Phe72/Tyr125/Asp99/Arg104, ΔG -16.9, Kd 1.2 nM, pLDDT 95.1) and a 'ZO-1 tight junction protector' (Arg220/Asp310, ΔG -16.1, Kd 2.8 nM, pLDDT 93.8). One sequence cannot have two different pLDDTs and cannot plausibly be a selective binder of two unrelated folds. (2) That sequence contains 'B' at position 19. B is the IUPAC ambiguity code for Asx (Asn or Asp); it is not a residue, cannot be synthesised, and is rejected by AlphaFold Server input validation — so the advertised 'Copy FASTA → Launch AlphaFold Server' workflow (index.html:362-363) fails outright for three of the entries. (3) AstroPafr-Block-A4's 'sequence' field is the string 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'. It is rendered under the modal heading '2. Sequence Structure (FASTA Peptide / Bio-Conjugate Sequence)' (index.html:619) and then fed to the confidence chart, which plots 37 points labelled H1, i2, s3, 14, 45, -6, P7, h8 … and reports a mean 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT' of 94.08 for the ASCII codes of an English phrase. (4) The PAE canvas is 540x220 px for a square N×N matrix (2.45x aspect distortion) and grid size is silently capped at 45, so the 99-residue lead candidate is truncated without notice. Consequence: Defect (3) is the single most efficient demonstration that no model is behind the charts, and it is visible to any user who clicks the A4 card — this is how the project gets discovered rather than disclosed. Defect (1) means the 25-candidate 'pipeline' is not 25 distinct designs; the duplication with divergent annotations is the pattern integrity officers look for when assessing whether a dataset was assembled or invented. Defect (2) breaks the one genuinely honest feature the platform has. Collectively these make the dataset unusable as a design record even for the author's own purposes.

text: Required fix for INTEG-07: Add a validation function that runs on load and refuses to render any record whose `sequence` is not `/^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$/`; surface the failure in the UI rather than silently plotting it. Replace 'B' with the intended residue (N or D) and re-derive anything downstream. Give A4 a real sequence or mark it explicitly 'small-molecule conjugate — no peptide component; structural prediction not applicable' and suppress the 3D/pLDDT/PAE panels for it. Deduplicate: either merge the four duplicate pairs into single records with multiple annotated indications, or design genuinely distinct sequences. Make the PAE canvas square and remove the silent gridSize cap (or label 'showing residues 1-45 of N').

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Ground truth for INTEG-07: FASTA sequences for structure prediction must use the 20 standard one-letter codes (optionally U/O for selenocysteine/pyrrolysine); B (Asx), Z (Glx), J (Xle) and X are ambiguity codes and are rejected or coerced by prediction pipelines. A PAE matrix is square N×N by definition and must be rendered with 1:1 aspect. A design record should carry one row per distinct construct, with a stable identifier, and distinct constructs should not share a sequence.

text: [MAJOR] Reference natural-product SMILES are wrong or unparseable, showing the curated reference layer was not retrieved from any chemical database — I parsed all eight SMILES strings and compared heavy-atom counts against PubChem records I retrieved this session. Curcumin (app.js:50) ends in 'OCH3', which is not valid SMILES — a bare H is illegal in the organic subset, so no cheminformatics toolkit will parse the string at all. Huperzine A (app.js:10) encodes 14 carbons against the true C15H18N2O (PubChem CID 854026). Ginsenoside Rg1 (app.js:20) encodes 38 carbons against C42H72O14 (CID 441923). Ginkgolide B (app.js:30) encodes C18O8 against C20H24O10 (CID 11973122). Two of the eight fields (app.js:60, 70) contain a molecular formula plus a prose annotation rather than a SMILES at all, yet are displayed to the user under the heading 'SMILES Formulation'. Only Baicalein and Asiatic Acid match on atom count (and Baicalein's hydroxyl regiochemistry differs from PubChem CID 5281605, which places OH at 5,6,7 — worth a separate chemistry check). No stereochemistry is specified anywhere, despite six of the eight being stereochemically defined natural products where configuration determines target engagement. Consequence: The natural-product matrix is the part of the platform that could have been fully correct at zero cost, because all eight compounds have authoritative public records. That it is not correct tells a reviewer the reference data was written from memory rather than retrieved — which retroactively lowers confidence in every other unsourced number on the page, including the ones that cannot be checked against a database. Anyone who copies these SMILES into a docking run or a similarity search gets the wrong molecule and does not find out.

text: Required fix for INTEG-08: Replace all eight SMILES with the isomeric SMILES retrieved from PubChem, and store the CID alongside each so the value is traceable: `{ smiles: "...", smiles_source: "PubChem", cid: 969516, retrieved: "2026-08-16" }`. Render the CID as a link next to the structure. Add a build-time validation step (RDKit `MolFromSmiles` non-null and formula match against the recorded CID) so an unparseable or mismatched SMILES fails CI. For Onjisaponin V and Salvianolic acid B, either supply the real SMILES or rename the field 'Molecular formula' so the label matches the content.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: [MINOR] 'Cognitive Enhancement Index (CEI)' is plotted as a computational benchmark and used to rank candidates, but is defined nowhere — A metric named 'Cognitive Enhancement Index', scored out of 100, is displayed as a leaderboard column and charted under the heading 'Computational Benchmark'. It has no definition in the repository: no inputs, no formula, no normalisation, no validation set, and no reference. The values also track the rank order almost perfectly (98.4 down to 82.5 for ranks 1-10), which suggests the score was written to match a pre-decided ranking rather than the ranking being derived from the score. Consequence: Calling something a 'benchmark' asserts that a defined, reproducible quantity was measured. An undefined composite score presented in a ranked table is unfalsifiable — a reader cannot check it, disagree with its weighting, or reproduce it, but will still use it to prioritise. It is a small item next to the pLDDT and ΔG problems, but it is the same failure mode and is trivially fixable.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Required fix for INTEG-09: Either (a) define it explicitly on the page — e.g. 'CEI = 0.4·norm(|ΔG|) + 0.3·norm(pLDDT) + 0.3·(target-class weight); an author-assigned heuristic, not a validated metric' — with the code that computes it from the other fields rather than a hardcoded literal, or (b) rename the column 'Author priority (subjective)' and change the chart heading from 'Computational Benchmark' to 'Author prioritisation vs ΔG'.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Ground truth for INTEG-09: A composite index used for ranking must state its constituent variables, their weights, their normalisation, and the rationale for the weighting; if it is model-derived, DOME (Walsh et al., Nat Methods 2021) requires the data, optimisation and evaluation to be reported. If it is a judgement-based scorecard, that is legitimate — it simply has to be labelled as expert judgement rather than as a computational benchmark.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3 (2024). The definitive specification of what AlphaFold 3 does and does not output. I retrieved the abstract and searched the Europe PMC full text: the confidence head 'predict[s] a modified local distance difference test (pLDDT) and a predicted aligned error (PAE) matrix as in AF2, as well as a distance error matrix (PDE)', plus pTM/ipTM ranking scores. There is no energetic output of any kind — no ΔG, no Kd, no IC50, no ADMET. Application here: This is the ground truth that settles INTEG-01 and INTEG-02. Cite it in the README and state plainly which of its outputs the project uses. It also fixes the pLDDT colour bins the UI advertises: the paper's own convention is pLDDT ≤50 / 50-70 / 70-90 / 90-100, so if the synthetic curve can never leave [89, 99] (app.js:791), the four-bin legend at index.html:388-391 must go or the data must change.

source.ref: doi:10.1038/s41592-021-01205-4 (PMID 34316068, Nature Methods 18:1122-1127); see also the DOME Registry, doi:10.1093/gigascience/giae094 (PMID 39661723, 2024)

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: DOME: recommendations for supervised machine learning validation in biology (2021). The community reporting standard for any ML-derived claim in biology, organised as Data, Optimization, Model, Evaluation. It exists precisely to make the question 'where did this number come from, and how would I check it?' answerable in a fixed format, and the 2024 Registry paper provides a machine-readable schema and public deposition route. Application here: Adopt DOME as the disclosure skeleton for the platform. For every model-derived value the repository must be able to fill in the four sections; where it cannot (which is currently everywhere), the value is by definition not model-derived and must be labelled 'illustrative'. Depositing a DOME Registry entry once a real AF3 run exists would give the project an external, citable provenance record at near-zero cost.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods (2024). The reporting standard governing any prediction intended to inform a clinical or health decision, including explicit items on data provenance, model specification, performance with uncertainty intervals, and — critically — a requirement to state the intended use and limitations rather than presenting point estimates bare. Application here: The '0% Risk' hERG claim and the efficacy percentages (INTEG-03, INTEG-04) are health-decision-relevant predictions. TRIPOD+AI is the standard a reviewer would hold them to, and it makes the necessary remediation concrete: every predicted quantity needs an uncertainty interval and an applicability-domain statement, and 'zero risk' is not a reportable prediction under any item of the checklist.

source.ref: FDA final guidance, issued 16 Nov 2023; Federal Register 17 Nov 2023, doc 2023-25470; docket FDA-2021-D-0980; fda.gov/media/154985/download

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Assessing the Credibility of Computational Modeling and Simulation in Medical Device Submissions: Guidance for Industry and Food and Drug Administration Staff (built on ASME V&V 40-2018) (2023). The regulatory framework for when computational output may be used as evidence: define the context of use, assess model risk (influence of the model on the decision × consequence of a wrong decision), then generate verification, validation and uncertainty-quantification evidence proportionate to that risk. It formalises the ASME V&V 40 credibility-factor approach. Application here: This is the vocabulary that lets the project stay ambitious while becoming honest. Every value gets a stated context of use and a model-risk tier. Under this framework a value used only to lay out a UI is low-risk and needs almost no credibility evidence — but it must be *declared* as such. A value used to claim '0% cardiotoxicity' in a human-cognition candidate is high-risk and needs V&V evidence the project does not have, so the correct action is to withdraw the claim rather than caveat it. I confirmed the guidance via official FDA and Federal Register listings; direct full-text fetch was blocked by the hosts.

source.ref: icmje.org/recommendations — Publishing and Editorial Issues, section B (retrieved and read this session)

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: ICMJE Recommendations for the Conduct, Reporting, Editing, and Publication of Scholarly Work in Medical Journals — section 'B. Scientific Misconduct, Expressions of Concern, and Retraction' (2025). The operative definition an editor or integrity officer would apply: scientific misconduct includes 'data fabrication; data falsification including deceptive manipulation of images; purposeful failure to disclose relationships and activities; and plagiarism', with editor obligations to investigate, inform institutions and funders, and issue expressions of concern or retraction. Application here: This is the standard that determines whether the current state is a legitimate prototype or an integrity problem, and the answer turns entirely on labelling. Formula-generated placeholders labelled as placeholders are not fabrication. The same values labelled 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score' and 'All 25 candidates underwent rigorous computational safety screening' would be assessed as fabricated data the moment the artefact is submitted, presented, or published. Fix the labels before the artefact leaves the author's machine and the exposure disappears entirely.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship (2016). Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable — in particular principle R1.2, that data must be associated with detailed provenance, and R1.1, that data carry a clear and accessible usage licence. Application here: FAIR R1.2 is the direct justification for the mandatory per-value provenance field proposed in the remediation standard. It also covers the natural-product layer (INTEG-08): recording a PubChem CID and retrieval date next to every SMILES makes the reference data findable and reusable, and turns an unverifiable string into a traceable one.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: A structural basis for drug-induced long QT syndrome (2000). The primary evidence identifying Tyr652 and Phe656 in the hERG S6 inner cavity as the residues that mediate high-affinity drug block, and establishing that aromatic/hydrophobic interaction with those residues is what confers hERG liability. Application here: The README names the right residues but inverts their meaning (INTEG-03). This citation is the ground truth showing that hydrophobicity and aromatic content increase rather than prevent hERG binding — directly contradicting 'Hydrophobic peptide linkers sterically prevent binding to hERG pore Tyr652/Phe656 residues' (README.md:99) for sequences I measured at net charge +9 with 31% W/F/Y content.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: De novo design of protein structure and function with RFdiffusion (2023). The current reference standard for what an honest de novo binder-design pipeline reports: a generative design stage, an in-silico filter with a stated metric and threshold, and — decisively — experimental success rates from the wet lab, including the failures. Application here: This is the template for keeping the project's ambition while making it credible. Restructure the 25 candidates as 'designs generated, filtered by [named metric] at [threshold], N selected for synthesis, 0 tested to date' rather than as 25 validated therapeutics with affinities and safety profiles. Reporting a design funnel with an honest zero at the experimental stage reads as serious work; reporting 25 finished candidates with -19.5 kcal/mol affinities and 0% risk does not.

tags: Research integrity, scientific claim substantiation, and computational-model credibility (in-silico drug discovery)
text: Benchmarking AlphaFold-enabled molecular docking predictions for antibiotic discovery (2022). Empirical demonstration that high-confidence AlphaFold structures do not translate into reliable ligand-binding predictions — docking against AF models gave poor agreement with experimental ligand-binding measurements, with no useful correlation between structural confidence and binding prediction accuracy. Application here: Pre-empts the most likely defence of the current design, namely 'high pLDDT justifies the affinity numbers'. It does not: structural confidence and binding energetics are decoupled. Cite this in the README's limitations section to explain why pLDDT is reported separately from, and never used to license, any affinity claim.
